styles.label: Procedural Neutral-Descriptive
styles.description: Primarily procedural or descriptive statements without substantive moral argument.

styles.label: Formal Ceremonial Address
styles.description: Formulaic greetings, speaker-address language, and protocol-centered rhetoric.

styles.label: Factual/Technical Reporting
styles.description: Technocratic exposition emphasizing facts, administration, and policy mechanics.

styles.label: Legal-Institutional Reasoning
styles.description: Arguments grounded in laws, institutions, constitutional constraints, and procedure.

styles.label: Rights-Based Deontological Appeal
styles.description: Moral claims framed as duties, rights, and non-negotiable obligations.

styles.label: Fairness-Equality-Justice Frame
styles.description: Reasoning centered on distributive fairness, equality, and justice norms.

styles.label: Consequentialist Cost-Benefit
styles.description: Evaluation based on likely outcomes, trade-offs, and aggregate social consequences.

styles.label: Welfare-State Solidarity Frame
styles.description: Collective solidarity, social protection, and public responsibility rhetoric.

styles.label: Market-Efficiency Competitiveness Frame
styles.description: Economic-efficiency, productivity, and competitiveness-oriented argumentation.

styles.label: Public Safety and Security Frame
styles.description: Threat minimization and societal safety as central argumentative focus.

styles.label: Humanitarian-Compassion Frame
styles.description: Empathy, vulnerability, and care for affected populations drive the reasoning.

styles.label: Victim-Protection Frame
styles.description: Prioritizes protection of victims and vulnerable groups as core moral imperative.

styles.label: Law-and-Order Punitive Frame
styles.description: Emphasis on deterrence, punishment, tougher enforcement, and sanctions.

styles.label: Preventive-Rehabilitation Frame
styles.description: Focus on prevention, reintegration, and long-term rehabilitation outcomes.

styles.label: Democratic Values and Rule-of-Law Frame
styles.description: Appeals to democracy, legitimacy, rights institutions, and constitutional norms.

styles.label: National Sovereignty Frame
styles.description: Prioritizes state autonomy, border/control authority, and national self-determination.

styles.label: Anti-Authoritarian Moral Condemnation
styles.description: Explicit moral condemnation of repressive regimes and rights violations.

styles.label: Adversarial Blame/Attack
styles.description: Opposition-focused attack rhetoric, blame assignment, and moralized political confrontation.

styles.label: Pragmatic Compromise/Consensus
styles.description: Negotiation-oriented style emphasizing compromise and workable middle-ground solutions.

styles.label: Evidence-Statistics-Expert Reference
styles.description: Justification through data points, expert authority, and empirical claims.

styles.label: Historical Analogy/Ideological Warning
styles.description: Uses historical examples or ideological comparisons to warn against current choices.

styles.label: Moral Polarization (Black-and-White)
styles.description: Binary moral framing where positions are cast as clearly right vs wrong.

styles.label: Identity Us-vs-Them Polarization
styles.description: In-group/out-group framing that emphasizes identity boundaries and conflict.
